src/kotoba-client-runtime.js.reason:
KOTOBA-158: the consent dialog's close listener denied whatever request was pending, so a late close event from an already-approved request auto-denied the next operation. The host now counts the closes it issues and ignores the matching events; an external close still denies. KOTOBA-159 (independent review findings 2, 4, 5, 6): only headers and body are taken from the caller's init, the sent Request is rebuilt from its URL with mode cors and cache no-store, and method-override headers are refused; a prefix route refuses `;` in the path; connect-src lists HTTP endpoint origins only; connect-src validates and reads one frozen copy of the descriptor. KOTOBA-159 finding 3 (owner decision 2026-10-31): Allow is disabled and does not count until the dialog has been showing for 600 ms, and then only for a trusted pointerdown or Enter/Space keydown on Allow that starts after that; the delay restarts for each request. KOTOBA-159: guest close interrupts request-body snapshot and pending consent, prevents later dispatch and signals in-flight fetch; a completed subsequent iframe navigation also closes the session; navigation start and already-started actions remain outside that guarantee. Nothing else in the file changes. KOTOBA-159: observe host DOM removals and abort detached sessions; require a connected container in the host document outside shadow DOM. Observation is asynchronous and does not reverse dispatched operations. KOTOBA-159: session abort also interrupts bounded guest response-body reads. JUN-751: accept memory as an explicit volatile local-state adapter; no operation or consent semantics change. KOTOBA-159 second review (2026-11-16) R1: the abort signal is carried by the approved Request instead of a fetch init, because a non-empty init resets the Request's referrer policy and the snapshot's no-referrer was lost. R2: a response refused after fetch (undeclared final origin, unverifiable redirect, failed artifact download) is cancelled. AWAI-325: explicit literal-IP/PeerID/protocol/byte/deadline-scoped libp2p host endpoints; canonical fresh consent, immutable payload/handler capture, cancellation and bounded responses; no HTTP origin fabrication or CSP widening. KOTOBA-159 R6: the restricted guest document starts with a script that removes RTCPeerConnection and webkitRTCPeerConnection, because CSP cannot stop WebRTC egress; Chromium only. AWAI-3001: bounded snapshot CID/transfer/listener/duration scopes, explicit read-back consent defaulting false, and literal-IP Relay v2 circuit addresses; preserve main review fixes. AWAI-3059: add the `transport: nearby` discovery profile (action advertise/browse/connect/send, bearers nsd/ble/wifi-direct/wifi-aware, 1 MiB budgets, deadline up to 120 s) with no PeerID, address or origin; payloads carry one declared bearer, a discovered peer token for connect/send and data only for send; it shares the peerAdapters capture, deadline, abort signal and response budget, shows nearby details in the consent modal and never enters connect-src. prepareClientOperationRequest and clientEndpointAllowsRequest refuse any endpoint that declares a transport. AWAI-3307: artifacts may declare `delivery: 'host-stream'` (byte budget up to 64 GiB). The broker then streams the body to a host sink captured at creation (`artifactSinks`), refusing before consent when none is supported, with an incremental SHA-256 (`createSha256`), the byte budget and a 60 s idle deadline; it calls the sink's close only on an exact digest match and abort otherwise. The consent dialog lists artifact revision, SHA-256, byte budget and delivery. In-memory artifacts keep the 512 MiB limit and `verifyClientArtifact` refuses host-stream declarations. AWAI-3336: a browser-action endpoint may name `recipient: 'user-selected-app'` instead of an origin, for a hand-off whose receiver the user picks in the OS (share sheet). No origin is fabricated, it never enters connect-src, and HTTP options stay refused; the broker shows the receiver as user-chosen in the consent modal and keeps the existing adapter capture, plain-data copy and each-operation consent. KOTOBA-159 owner decisions 2026-11-22 (docs/client-runtime-review-20261122.md): finding 7, generic-network endpoints (wildcard/pattern origin, parameter-only path) are refused by shape as generic-network-endpoint; findings 8/P1/D1, loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, 0.0.0.0/8, LAN names and IPv6 equivalents (::1, fc00::/7, fe80::/10, IPv4-mapped/compatible, NAT64) in service, browser-action and redirect origins, peer addresses, relay hops and the receive listener need operation scope 'lan', shown in the dialog (clientAddressScope); finding 9, every operation carries a validated disclosure (recipient legal name, country, data in words, special-care with kinds, purpose, frequency, withdrawal; foreign country name and 施行規則 17 条 2 項 page) shown on the dialog's first screen in Legal's draft wording (CLIENT_CONSENT_TEXT, status draft, ja/en), with scope and payload summary (type, size, SHA-256, field names, header names, text) behind 詳細を見る; finding 1, trusted-page-v1 says the screen does not guarantee restriction and uses 閉じる/続ける, only restricted-wasm-v1 says refusing sends nothing; equal-weight choices with no default focus; R3, one broker slot taken before snapshot and released when consent resolves; R4, mountRestrictedClientApp accepts only brokers recorded in a private WeakSet; R5/D4, fixed fields above Action, query length, 160-character cut with a 全文 toggle; D2, scoped peer adapters must declare kotoba.peer-scope-enforcement.v1, the broker checks max-transfer-bytes against PEER_TRANSFER_MAX_BYTES and the declared bound, and verifyPeerAdapterScopeConformance is the host conformance helper. KOTOBA-159 App QA 2026-11-22: each notice paragraph is its own

(A); the details blocks carry inline wrapping styles so they stay inside the dialog without the stylesheet (B); the controls get tabindex 0 and Tab / Shift+Tab cycle inside the modal, skipping Allow while it is disabled (C).
